_what_this_is: RULINGS, not defects and not open work. One row per decision that has been ROUTED to an owner and is waiting on that owner to either act or decline -- with the decline recorded as a decision rather than left as silence. It exists because a routed finding has no state anywhere: docs/defect-density-register.json records defects that were FIXED, docs/known-red-suites.json records suites that FAIL, and neither can say 'this was handed to somebody and nobody has answered'.
_why_a_register_and_not_a_document: A routing document is written once and then re-written the next time somebody notices the item is still open -- which is how tools/hover_auditor_scope_gate.py:409 came to be routed TWICE, in b10 and again in b11, with the second routing's only new content being 'this is the second routing'. A row with an owner and a state is read in one line and cannot be accidentally re-derived.

_the_states.DECIDE_OR_NOT_PROMOTED: The owner must either DO the thing or record a NOT_PROMOTED entry in tools/report_only_checks.py saying why it should not exist. BOTH ARE ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS. What this state refuses is the third option -- neither done nor declined, for batch after batch.
_the_states.DONE: Acted on. Carries the commit that did it.
_the_states.NOT_PROMOTED: Declined, with the reason recorded in tools/report_only_checks.NOT_PROMOTED. A decline is a result.
_the_states.SUPERSEDED: Overtaken by something else. Carries what replaced it.

_what_this_register_does_NOT_claim: That the owner has READ the row. There is no reply channel on this platform, and that absence is the reason a state field is the best available substitute -- it is a place the owner can answer in one token. A row sitting at DECIDE_OR_NOT_PROMOTED means nobody has answered, NOT that nobody looked.
_how_acknowledgement_is_measured: scratchpad/ack_check.py, which reads the routing documents as the population and looks for four signals -- a commit on origin/main touching the file after the routing, an ACTIVE claim naming it, the owner's status-registry row naming it, or a NOT_PROMOTED entry naming the FILE AND THE LINE. Its first version matched a bare basename in NOT_PROMOTED prose and reported two FALSE acknowledgements; that is fixed and the state MENTION_ONLY now exists for exactly that case.
merge_policy: APPEND-ONLY on `rulings`, keyed by `id`. A conflict is resolved as a UNION of both sides' rows; two rows with the same id are a defect and the older one wins, because a ruling that was recorded first is the one other documents already cite.

rulings.subject: tools/hover_auditor_scope_gate.py:409
rulings.title: the 4th instance of the unfetched-base shape, plus the checker that would stop a 5th
rulings.what_decides_it: EITHER apply the :402-:409 replacement written out in the b10 routing document and build the specified checker, OR record a NOT_PROMOTED entry in tools/report_only_checks.py saying why neither should exist. A NOT_PROMOTED decision is a perfectly good answer and is the preferred one if the view is that a gate exiting early in every build clone is not worth hardening.
rulings.why_it_is_not_urgent: tools/hover_auditor_scope_gate.py runs FIRST in .githooks/pre-push and exits before the range matters in a build clone, so it has passed every push attempt and blocks nobody. That is also exactly why it will stay unfixed unless somebody decides -- an item that never hurts is an item nothing forces.

evidence.worst_symptom_of_the_shape: not a refusal but a FALSE FINDING: NO OWNER: 4 over four pre-existing shared tools, with 'add an # OWNER: line' as the printed remedy, which would have had one session write itself as owner of two contested files to get an unrelated push out.
evidence.acknowledgement_state_when_recorded: MENTION_ONLY per scratchpad/ack_check.py -- the basename appears in NOT_PROMOTED prose about a different subject, and nothing names line 409.
